newsitem.title: USA: Fed expected to add via 3-day system repurchases.
newsitem.headline: Fed expected to add via 3-day system repurchases.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Monday through three-day system repurchase agreements, analysts said.
"I'm looking for a small, three-day fixed system repurchase," said Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston.
"We're looking for three-day system RPs," said Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities America Inc. He said the Fed had not met all of its reserve needs.
Analysts estimated that the Fed faces an average daily add need of about $6.0 billion in reserves in the current bank reserve maintenance period which began on July 3.
The Fed added $4.885 billion in temporary reserves to the banking system through seven-day fixed system repurchase agreements on Thursday.
"Our numbers show a $6.0 billion add need and they did not keep pace with that with the seven-day system RP," said Moran.
Federal funds were trading at 5-1/2 percent, the Fed's target for the rate, in early dealings.
